sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，《纽约时报》.

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》.

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是.

sentences.en: For seven years, they've waited for the chance to dismantle President Obama's Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 七年来，他们一直在等待机会来废除奥巴马总统的《平价医疗法案》.

sentences.en: So why are some Republicans now revolting against the Republican plan to replace it?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么现在一些共和党人却在抗拒旨在取代它的共和党计划呢？

sentences.en: We take a close look at the bill to understand, and we call a former Republican presidential candidate for his take.
sentences.zh: 我们深入研究了这项法案以了解究竟，并邀请了一位前共和党总统候选人谈谈他的看法.

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, March 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月8日，星期三.

sentences.en: Yes, Truman, President and President-elect, comes before Congress.
sentences.zh: 是的，杜鲁门，这位总统兼当选总统，来到了国会面前.

sentences.en: The State of the Union, he says, is good.
sentences.zh: 他说，国情良好.

sentences.en: We begin in 1948.
sentences.zh: 我们从1948年开始讲起.

sentences.en: The greatest gap in our social security structure is the lack of adequate provision for the nation's health.
sentences.zh: 我们社会保障体系中最大的漏洞，是缺乏对国民健康充足的保障.

sentences.en: We are rightly proud of the high standards of medical care we know how to provide in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们为美国所拥有的高标准医疗服务水平感到自豪.

sentences.en: The fact is, however, that most of our people cannot afford to pay for the care they need.
sentences.zh: 然而事实是，我们的大多数民众承担不起他们所需的医疗费用.

sentences.en: And so it began.
sentences.zh: 事情就这样开始了.

sentences.en: This great nation cannot afford to allow its citizens to suffer needlessly from the lack of proper medical care.
sentences.zh: 这个伟大的国家不能容忍其公民由于缺乏适当的医疗服务而遭受不必要的痛苦.

sentences.en: Like dozens of allies after the Second World War, the United States started to debate whether to create a nationwide health care system.
sentences.zh: 就像二战后的几十个盟友一样，美国开始讨论是否建立一个全国性的医疗保健系统.

sentences.en: By July of that year, Britain had a national health care program.
sentences.zh: 到那年7月，英国已经拥有了一个国民医疗保健计划.

sentences.en: And soon enough, similar programs were enacted in Sweden, Iceland, Norway, Denmark, and Finland.
sentences.zh: 很快，瑞典、冰岛、挪威、丹麦和芬兰也通过了类似的计划.

sentences.en: Then, Japan, Canada, Italy, and China.
sentences.zh: 然后是日本、加拿大、意大利和中国.

sentences.en: By the end of the 1970s, the idea had spread through much of the industrialized world.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪70年代末，这一理念已传遍了大部分工业化世界.

sentences.en: In the United States, programs like Medicare and Medicaid were developed to protect specific groups, like the elderly or the poor.
sentences.zh: 在美国，诸如医疗保险（Medicare）和医疗救助（Medicaid）之类的计划是为了保护特定群体而发展起来的，例如老年人或穷人.

sentences.en: But because of its size, because of its history, because of its nature, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但由于其规模、历史和本质，美国

sentences.en: never enacted such sweeping legislation until 2010.
sentences.zh: 从未颁布过如此庞大的立法，直到2010年.

sentences.en: Today, after almost a century of trying, today, after over a year of debate, today, after all the votes have been tallied,
sentences.zh: 今天，在经历了近一个世纪的尝试之后，今天，在经过了一年多的辩论之后，今天，在所有选票清点完毕之后，

sentences.en: health insurance reform becomes law in the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 医疗保险改革在美国正式成为法律.

sentences.en: But, as soon as it was signed, before it was signed,
sentences.zh: 但是，就在它被签署的同时，甚至在它被签署之前，

sentences.en: It's in our government, and we're going to rip it out.
sentences.zh: 它就在我们的政府里，而我们要把它连根拔起.

sentences.en: Opponents of the bill began to cry for repeal.
sentences.zh: 该法案的反对者开始发出废除的呼声.

sentences.en: In no uncertain terms, repeal this bill.
sentences.zh: 用明确无误的措辞，废除这个法案.

sentences.en: And after seven years and more than 60 attempts to repeal, Republicans have now won control of the House, the Senate, and the presidency.
sentences.zh: 在经历了七年和60多次废除尝试之后，共和党人现在赢得了对众议院、参议院和总统职位的控制.

sentences.en: Their moment to do what they've longed to do has come.
sentences.zh: 他们期盼已久的时刻终于到来了.

sentences.en: But recently, something has changed.
sentences.zh: 但最近，情况发生了一些变化.

sentences.en: Really, I think what we're seeing right now is a debate within the Republican Party about what is their vision for health care and does this bill represent it well.
sentences.zh: 真的，我认为我们现在看到的是共和党内部的一场辩论，关于他们对医疗保健的愿景是什么，以及这项法案是否很好地体现了这一点.

sentences.en: Margot Sanger-Katz has been reporting on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 玛戈·桑格-卡茨多年来一直在报道美国的

sentences.en: health care system for years.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健系统.

sentences.en: Margot, real quick before we get into the new bill, remind us, what is the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 玛戈，在我们讨论新法案之前，简单提醒一下，什么是《平价医疗法案》？

sentences.en: The Affordable Care Act was this big, sprawling, complex piece of legislation that was designed to help people who couldn't afford to buy their own insurance
sentences.zh: 《平价医疗法案》是一项庞大、杂乱且复杂的立法，旨在帮助那些买不起自己保险的人

sentences.en: have the ability to get access to it.
sentences.zh: 获得购买保险的能力.

sentences.en: And it was also designed to make sure that people who were shut out of the old insurance system because they had prior illnesses no longer were excluded.
sentences.zh: 它还旨在确保那些因以前患病而被旧保险体系排除在外的人不再遭到排斥.

sentences.en: In the simplest terms, how is this new health care plan from the Republicans different from the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 用最简单的术语来说，共和党人的这个新医疗计划与《平价医疗法案》有何不同？

sentences.en: Oh, that's a hard question to answer.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一个很难回答的问题.

sentences.en: The Affordable Care Act took our dysfunctional health care system and, like, layered some stuff on top of it.
sentences.zh: 《平价医疗法案》接受了我们功能失调的医疗体系，并在其之上叠加了一些东西.

sentences.en: This Republican, you know, repeal, replace, reform, whatever we want to call it, is doing some of the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你懂的，共和党这个废除、替代、改革，无论我们怎么称呼它，也在做类似的事情.

sentences.en: You know, when the Affordable Care Act was first passed and in the years afterwards, and I guess really right up until very recently.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当《平价医疗法案》刚通过以及随后的几年里，我想实际上直到不久前都是如此.

sentences.en: So our plan, repeal it, clean repeal.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的计划是，废除它，彻底废除.

sentences.en: The battle cry was, we're going to repeal Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 当时的战斗口号是，我们要废除奥巴马医改.

sentences.en: Complete repeal, clean repeal.
sentences.zh: 完全废除，彻底废除.

sentences.en: And I think what Republicans really meant is, like, we want to go back to the old health care system that we had in 2009,
sentences.zh: 我认为共和党人真正的意思是，我们想回到2009年时我们拥有的旧医疗体系，

sentences.en: where we didn't have this huge expansion of government benefits and we didn't have this, you know, extensive regulation of health insurance.
sentences.zh: 当时我们没有这种政府福利的大幅扩张，也没有对医疗保险的广泛监管.

sentences.en: But since then, people have kind of gotten used to this new system.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，人们有点习惯了这个新系统.

sentences.en: And we have, you know, more than 20 million people who are newly insured as a result of it.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，由于这项法案，有超过2000万人获得了新保险.

sentences.en: And so I think it's become much politically harder for Republicans to just say, we're going to turn back the clock.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，对于共和党人来说，单纯说我们要开倒车在政治上变得更加困难了.

sentences.en: And so this bill, the American Health Care Act, instead, they've moved to this idea that we're going to repeal and replace Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 所以这项法案，即《美国医疗法案》，他们转而提出了我们要废除并取代奥巴马医改的想法.

sentences.en: It keeps our promise to repeal and replace Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 它兑现了我们废除并取代奥巴马医改的承诺.

sentences.en: That's actually quite hard because I don't think that they have as clear a vision as the Democrats had of what they want the health care system to look like and how they're going to get there.
sentences.zh: 这实际上相当困难，因为我认为他们并没有像民主党那样清晰的愿景，不知道他们希望医疗体系变成什么样以及如何实现这一目标.

sentences.en: And so what we see with this bill is it just makes various changes to Obamacare's program, but it's not, like, structurally revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从这项法案中看到的是，它只是对奥巴马医改的计划做了各种修改，但它在结构上并不是革命性的.

sentences.en: It's just kind of – it's making changes to how things work.
sentences.zh: 它只是——它只是在改变事情的运作方式.

sentences.en: Let's talk about just a few of those changes and what are the biggest of them.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈其中一些改动以及其中最大的几项.

sentences.en: So the biggest one I would say is that it totally changes the nature of these tax credits that help people buy their own insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最大的一点是，它彻底改变了帮助人们购买自己保险的税收抵免的性质.

sentences.en: Under Obamacare, basically, your tax credit is calculated based on how much does insurance cost in your area and how much do you earn.
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马医改下，基本上你的税收抵免额是根据你所在地区的保险费用以及你的收入来计算的.

sentences.en: And then they sort of do some math and say, okay, you only have to pay a certain percentage of your income towards your premiuMs.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会做一些数学计算，然后说，好的，你只需要拿出收入的一定比例来支付保费.

sentences.en: And so what that means is that if you're pretty poor and health insurance is really expensive where you live, the amount you pay for the product is pretty low.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，如果你相当贫困，而你居住的地方医疗保险非常昂贵，那么你为该产品支付的金额其实很低.

sentences.en: And that's why so many poor people have signed up because the plans are really affordable.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有那么多穷人注册的原因，因为这些计划确实负担得起.

sentences.en: What the Republicans want to do is instead of having this complex formula, they want to say, like, if you're a certain age, you get a flat tax credit.
sentences.zh: 共和党人想要做的是，不再使用这种复杂的公式，而是说，如果你到了某个年龄，你就会得到固定的税收抵免.

sentences.en: If you're 20 years old, for example, you would get a tax credit that's $2,000.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你20岁，你将获得2000美元的税收抵免.

sentences.en: If you're older, if you're 60 years old, you get $4,000 and you can use that to buy insurance.
sentences.zh: 如果你年龄更大，如果你60岁，你将获得4000美元，你可以用它来买保险.

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter how much insurance costs in your area and it doesn't matter how poor or rich you are except at the very high end.
sentences.zh: 这与你所在地区的保险费用无关，也与你是穷人还是富人无关（极高收入阶层除外）。

sentences.en: And so what that means is that there are more Americans who are eligible for tax credits under this system than Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在这个系统下，有更多的美国人有资格获得税收抵免，超过了奥巴马医改.

sentences.en: But because they're not scaled to people's income, they end up being a lot less generous for particular groups of people and a lot more generous for others.
sentences.zh: 但因为它们没有根据人们的收入进行调整，最终对于特定群体来说变得没那么慷慨，而对其他人则慷慨得多.

sentences.en: I want to make sure I understand why poor people are not going to benefit from this new plan.
sentences.zh: 我想弄清楚为什么穷人不会从这个新计划中受益.

sentences.en: Well, I have an example here that I can share with you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我这里有一个例子可以与你分享.

sentences.en: So here's an example I looked up.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我查到的一个例子.

sentences.en: If you live in central Nebraska right now and you're 60 years old and you make $20,000, the tax credit that you're eligible for under Obamacare is worth about $18,500.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在住在内布拉斯加州中部，年龄60岁，收入20000美元，根据奥巴马医改，你有资格获得的税收抵免价值约18500美元.

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那是一大笔钱.

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那是一大笔钱.

sentences.en: Under the new plan, the tax credit that you're eligible for is worth $4,000.
sentences.zh: 根据新计划，你有资格获得的税收抵免价值4000美元.

sentences.en: And I don't think that the premiums that you're going to have to pay are so substantially different under this plan that it's going to make up for the $14,000 you've just lost in tax assistance.
sentences.zh: 我不认为在这个计划下你必须支付的保费会有如此巨大的差异，以至于能够弥补你刚刚在税务援助中失去的14000美元.

sentences.en: So if you're someone who earns $20,000 a year, it's not exactly clear to me where you're going to come up with $14,000 additional dollars in order to buy health insurance.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你是一个年收入20000美元的人，我并不太清楚你要去哪里凑齐额外的14000美元来购买医疗保险.

sentences.en: Probably if you're that person, you're going to go from having insurance to not having insurance.
sentences.zh: 如果你是那个人，你很可能会从有保险变成没有保险.

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧.

sentences.en: Then there's this big politically charged word, mandate.
sentences.zh: 接下来是这个充满政治色彩的大词：强制令（mandate）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的.

sentences.en: So it gets rid of the mandate.
sentences.zh: 所以它取消了强制令.

sentences.en: So that means if you don't want to have insurance, you don't have to and you don't have to pay a penalty.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你不想买保险，你就不必买，也不用支付罚款.

sentences.en: But it has a bunch of other policies in there that are designed to try to still encourage people to buy insurance.
sentences.zh: 但它里面还有一堆其他政策，旨在继续鼓励人们购买保险.

sentences.en: And the other thing it does is it creates this penalty if you get uninsured.
sentences.zh: 它做的另一件事是，如果你失去了保险，它会设定一种惩罚.

sentences.en: So if you drop your insurance and then you decide you want to buy some insurance later, like maybe when you get sick,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你退掉了保险，然后决定以后再买一些保险，比如在你生病的时候，

sentences.en: you have to pay 30 percent more than someone who's been insured the whole time.
sentences.zh: 你必须支付比一直有保险的人高出30%的费用.

sentences.en: And the Republicans say this will create a financial incentive for people to stay in the system over time.
sentences.zh: 共和党人表示，这将为人们随着时间推移留在体系内创造经济激励.

sentences.en: That sounds a lot like a penalty, like from the old plan.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很像罚款，就像旧计划里的一样.

sentences.en: It is, but it's also, you know, critics have pointed out that there are some weird perverse incentives that could occur as a result of this penalty.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这也是，你知道的，批评人士指出，这种罚款可能会产生一些奇怪的逆向激励.

sentences.en: So the individual mandate penalty you pay every year, you don't have insurance.
sentences.zh: 因此，个人强制令罚款是你每年没有保险时都要支付的.

sentences.en: And then as soon as you want to buy insurance, you just pay the normal price.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦你想买保险，你只需支付正常价格.

sentences.en: This penalty, you don't pay anything when you're uninsured.
sentences.zh: 而这种罚款，你在没有保险时不用支付任何费用.

sentences.en: And then when you go get insurance, that's when you have to pay this extra price.
sentences.zh: 然后当你去买保险时，那才是你必须支付这笔额外费用的时刻.

sentences.en: And so I think you have to imagine, like, what happens if you're a healthy person and I don't know, maybe you lose your job.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你必须想象一下，如果你是一个健康的人，我不知道，也许你失业了.

sentences.en: You can't afford insurance for a couple of months.
sentences.zh: 你有几个月买不起保险.

sentences.en: Then you decide you want to go buy it and you find out there's this big penalty.
sentences.zh: 然后你决定去买，结果发现有这么大一笔罚款.

sentences.en: It may be the case that you don't get insurance.
sentences.zh: 情况很可能是你干脆不买保险了.

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not going to get insurance until I'm sick.
sentences.zh: 是的，我才不在生病前买保险呢.

sentences.en: I can't afford this, you know, 130 percent of what everyone else is paying.
sentences.zh: 我承担不起这个，你知道的，相当于其他人支付的130%的费用.

sentences.en: The other big change is it really makes substantial changes to Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 另一个重大改变是，它对医疗救助（Medicaid）做出了实质性修改.

sentences.en: It pulls back some of the extra funding that the Affordable Care Act gave to states to cover the poor people that they didn't used to cover.
sentences.zh: 它撤回了《平价医疗法案》提供给各州的一些额外资金，用于覆盖以前没有覆盖到的穷人.

sentences.en: And then it also makes some changes to the structure of the program that over time are going to reduce federal spending on Medicaid and potentially could result in less care for poor people.
sentences.zh: 然后它还对该计划的结构进行了调整，随着时间的推移，这将减少联邦在医疗救助上的支出，并可能导致穷人获得的医疗护理减少.

sentences.en: How much does the new plan cost?
sentences.zh: 新计划花费多少？

sentences.en: We have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道.

sentences.en: How is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能？

sentences.en: The Republicans are really in a big hurry to pass this bill.
sentences.zh: 共和党人现在非常急于通过这项法案.

sentences.en: And so they're proceeding in their process without waiting for the Congressional Budget Office to do its calculations.
sentences.zh: 因此他们在推进程序时，并没有等待国会预算办公室进行测算.

sentences.en: At some point in the future,
sentences.zh: 在未来的某个时刻，

sentences.en: we are going to get this report and the report is going to include estimates of how many people are going to get or lose health insurance and how much it's going to cost federal taxpayers.
sentences.zh: 我们将得到这份报告，报告将包括关于有多少人会获得或失去医疗保险以及将花费联邦纳税人多少钱的估计.

sentences.en: But those numbers are not available at this time.
sentences.zh: 但目前这些数字还无法获得.

sentences.en: And Republicans are going to continue to move forward with this bill in the absence of those numbers.
sentences.zh: 在没有这些数字的情况下，共和党人将继续推进这项法案.

sentences.en: It feels, Margar, like there's no way to pull this new Republican law away from the really urgent politics that surround it.
sentences.zh: 玛戈，感觉似乎没有什么办法能让这个新的共和党法律摆脱围绕它的那些极为紧迫的政治压力.

sentences.en: Real change begins with immediately repealing and replacing the disaster known as Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 真正的变革始于立即废除并取代被称为灾难的奥巴马医改.

sentences.en: Ideally, the Republicans would have had more time to do this, but they've got the 100 days pressure since the election.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，共和党人本该有更多时间来做这件事，但他们面临着自大选以来的100天压力.

sentences.en: How much of what we're seeing here is just a response to enormous pressure to do something right now?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里看到的种种现象，有多少仅仅是对现在必须做点什么的巨大压力的反应？

sentences.en: I think there's like on the one hand, on the other hand here, on the one hand, yeah, you know, they haven't been in for that long.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点像一方面，另一方面，一方面，是的，你知道，他们上台并没有那么久.

sentences.en: They're the, you know, President Trump really put a lot of pressure on them to do this first before they did anything else.
sentences.zh: 他们是，你知道的，特朗普总统确实给他们施加了很大压力，让他们在做其他事情之前先把这个做完.

sentences.en: But he demanded like right away.
sentences.zh: 但他要求立即行动.

sentences.en: Yeah, he said right away.
sentences.zh: 是的，他说马上.

sentences.en: And he also said you have to do the whole thing all at once.
sentences.zh: 他还说你们必须一次性把整件事搞定.

sentences.en: We have to repeal and replace Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 我们必须废除并取代奥巴马医改.

sentences.en: You take a look at the kind of numbers that that will cost us in the year 17.
sentences.zh: 你看看这将在17年给我们带来什么样的成本数字.

sentences.en: It is a disaster.
sentences.zh: 这是一场灾难.

sentences.en: That's pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 这挺难的.

sentences.en: That's not that much time.
sentences.zh: 时间没那么多.

sentences.en: On the other hand, you know, Obamacare has been the law since 2010.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你知道，奥巴马医改自2010年以来一直都是法律.

sentences.en: Republicans have been railing against it and running against it and advertising against it for all of this time.
sentences.zh: 共和党人一直在对其进行抨击、竞选反对、并登广告反对，持续了这么长时间.

sentences.en: It is not as if they did not know what the law was and what the options were that were before them.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他们不知道法律是什么，也不知道他们面前有哪些选项.

sentences.en: And you could imagine a scenario in which they were just delighted to hand over the bill on day one because they had been thinking about it this whole time.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象这样一种情况，他们在第一天就乐意交出这项法案，因为他们一直在考虑这件事.

sentences.en: So, yeah, they're in a rush.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他们在赶时间.

sentences.en: But I think part of what the kind of slapdash nature of this process reflects is that Republicans really aren't in agreement about what it is they want to do on health care.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这个过程所表现出的那种草率性质，部分反映出共和党人在医疗保健方面到底想做什么并未达成一致.

sentences.en: And so that has led them to kind of scramble to try to assemble something that can appeal broadly to their entire caucus and also be written and scored and passed in this very abbreviated time frame.
sentences.zh: 因此，这导致他们不得不手忙脚乱地拼凑出一个方案，既能广泛吸引整个党团会议，又能在如此短的时间内完成编写、评估和通过.

sentences.en: Just how deep are the divisions within the Republican Party over this new health care plan?
sentences.zh: 对于这个新医疗计划，共和党内部的分歧到底有多深？

sentences.en: They're really, really deep.
sentences.zh: 真的很深，非常深.

sentences.en: And, you know, here are a couple of examples of things that they're fighting about that I think are sort of existential to the bill.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这里有几个他们正在争论的事情的例子，我认为这些事情对该法案来说具有生存攸关的意义.

sentences.en: There are a substantial number of conservatives who do not feel that the federal government should be giving people money to help them buy health insurance.
sentences.zh: 有相当数量的保守派认为，联邦政府不应该给人们钱来帮助他们购买医疗保险.

sentences.en: No one has a right to medical care, period.
sentences.zh: 没有人拥有获得医疗服务的天然权利，就这样.

sentences.en: Our government has been mismanaging medical care for more than 45 years.
sentences.zh: 我们的政府管理医疗服务不善已经超过45年了.

sentences.en: For every problem it has created, it has responded by exponentially expanding the role of government.
sentences.zh: 它每制造一个问题，其回应都是呈指数级扩大政府的角色.

sentences.en: That's one example.
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子.

sentences.en: Another is, you know, this Medicaid expansion has led to millions of low-income people getting coverage, many of them living in Republican states.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是，你知道，这个医疗救助（Medicaid）的扩张已经让数百万低收入人群获得了保障，他们当中许多人住在红州（共和党州）。

sentences.en: And so for particularly senators who come from those states, they don't want all of those people to lose their coverage.
sentences.zh: 因此，特别是对于来自这些州的参议员来说，他们不希望所有这些人失去医疗保障.

sentences.en: So even though they are theoretically in favor of repealing Obamacare,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他们在理论上赞成废除奥巴马医改，

sentences.en: I think they also really support this really crucial part of Obamacare that did involve a whole lot of federal spending and oversight.
sentences.zh: 我也认为他们同样非常支持奥巴马医改中这个至关重要的部分，即确实涉及大量联邦支出和监督的部分.

sentences.en: And so, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，

sentences.en: how do you thread the needle between people who feel the federal government shouldn't be in the business of giving health care to people or giving them money to get health care and people who feel like that millions of people should be able to have access to this government program?
sentences.zh: 你如何在那些认为联邦政府不该涉足为人提供医疗服务或给钱让人看病的人，与那些认为数百万人都应该能够获得这一政府项目的人之间，找到平衡点呢？

sentences.en: Good question.
sentences.zh: 好问题.

sentences.en: Margot, has something happened in the last seven years that in a way can't be undone in American health care?
sentences.zh: 玛戈，在过去的七年里，美国医疗保健领域是否发生了某种在某种程度上无法逆转的事情？

sentences.en: We're going to find out the answer to that question, but I think that the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 我们将找出这个问题的答案，但我认为答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: I really think that the Affordable Care Act has reset people's expectations about what the government's role is in helping people get health insurance and what kind of access to health insurance people ought to have.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为，《平价医疗法案》重新设定了人们对政府在帮助人们获得健康保险方面所起作用的预期，以及人们应该获得什么样的健康保险。

sentences.en: And I think we really see that reflected in President Trump's statements, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为我们在特朗普总统的声明中确实看到了这种反映。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: He's been saying all along that it's really important that we don't allow people to fall between the cracks.
sentences.zh: 他一直都在说，绝对不能让任何人落入无人照顾的境地，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: He was saying that even in the presidential primary, he said just after the election that it was really important that we have a plan that cover everyone.
sentences.zh: 他在总统初选时就这么说过，他在大选刚结束时也说过，制定一个覆盖所有人的计划非常重要。

sentences.en: Everybody's got to be covered.
sentences.zh: 每个人都必须得到保障。

sentences.en: This is an un-Republican thing for me to say, because a lot of times they say, no, no, the lower 25 percent, they can't afford private.
sentences.zh: 我说这话有点不像共和党人，因为很多时候他们会说，不，不，底层的25%买不起私人保险。

sentences.en: But universal health care.
sentences.zh: 但是全民医疗保健。

sentences.en: I am going to take care of everybody.
sentences.zh: 我会照顾每一个人。

sentences.en: I don't care if it costs me votes or not.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎这会不会让我失去选票。

sentences.en: Everybody's going to be taken care of much better than they're taken care of now.
sentences.zh: 每个人的生活都会得到照顾，比现在好得多。

sentences.en: These statements are really different than the kinds of things that Republicans were saying when the Affordable Care Act was debated, where they just basically were saying,
sentences.zh: 这些言论与当年辩论《平价医疗法案》时共和党人所说的话完全不同，他们当时基本上是在说，

sentences.en: get the government out of my health care.
sentences.zh: 别让政府插手我的医疗。

sentences.en: And that brings me to my final question, which is what is going to be the role of President Trump in getting this bill passed in making a major change to the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了我的最后一个问题，即特朗普总统在推动该法案通过、对《平价医疗法案》进行重大修改的过程中将扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: So far, it's not clear how enthusiastic he is about it.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他对此有多大热情还不得而知。

sentences.en: He, in a tweet, described it as our bill, but he also said that it is a starting place for negotiation.
sentences.zh: 他在一条推文中将之称为我们的法案，但他也说过，这是谈判的起点。

sentences.en: And his spokesman, Sean Spicer, made some similar comments today.
sentences.zh: 他的发言人肖恩·斯派塞今天也发表了类似的评论。

sentences.en: So I think the president has sort of like tentatively endorsed this plan, but he hasn't wholeheartedly endorsed this plan.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为总统对这个计划可以说是暂时赞同，但他并没有全心全意地支持。

sentences.en: So I think we really have to see whether he wants to bring all of his power to bear on trying to make this bill into law.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我们还得看看他是否愿意动用自己全部的力量，努力将这个法案变成法律。

sentences.en: Margot, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 玛戈，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Now, I have to tell you, it's an unbelievably complex subject.
sentences.zh: 现在，我必须告诉你，这是一个难以置信的复杂话题。

sentences.en: Nobody knew that health care could be so complicated.
sentences.zh: 谁也没想到医疗保健会这么复杂。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Thank you for taking a minute to watch this report to you about a very important new project at American Solutions.
sentences.zh: 感谢您花时间观看这份关于美国解决方案公司一个非常重要的新项目的报告。

sentences.en: If you go to nomoreobamacare.com, you can play a major role in helping stop the socialization of American health care,
sentences.zh: 如果您访问 nomoreobamacare.com，您就可以在阻止美国医疗体制走向社会主义、

sentences.en: the centralization, and the domination of your health choices by Washington bureaucrats.
sentences.zh: 以及阻止华盛顿官僚对您的健康选择进行集权化和主导方面发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: We have a project now to get people to sign a petition to get their senators to vote to repeal Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有一个项目，旨在号召人们签署请愿书，促使参议员投票废除奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: That was former Republican Speaker of the House, Newt Gingrich, six years ago.
sentences.zh: 那是六年前的前共和党众议院议长纽特·金里奇。

sentences.en: After hearing the details of the new health plan, I called him up.
sentences.zh: 在听取了新医疗计划的细节后，我给他打了电话。

sentences.en: Hello, sir.
sentences.zh: 你好，先生。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 好的，先生。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: What's up?
sentences.zh: 什么事？

sentences.en: So many Republicans are criticizing this new health care bill as an establishment bill.
sentences.zh: 许多共和党人都在批评这个新的医疗法案是一个建制派法案。

sentences.en: They're saying it's too close to President Obama's original health care bill.
sentences.zh: 他们说这太接近奥巴马总统最初的医疗法案了。

sentences.en: There's a leadership plan that was brought forward, which I believe, when you look through it, is Obamacare in a different form.
sentences.zh: 有一项被提交上来的领导层计划，我相信，如果你仔细研究一下，它就是换汤不换药的奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: What do you think of their critique?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待他们的批评？

sentences.en: Are they correct?
sentences.zh: 他们说得对吗？

sentences.en: No, I think this bill has to be seen as the first of either three or four bills, and therefore it will not satisfy someone who wants a full-blown repeal.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这个法案必须被视为三到四个法案中的第一个，因此它无法满足那些想要全面废除的人。

sentences.en: But to get something to the Senate when you only have 52 senators, I think you have to write a narrower bill and then come back this fall
sentences.zh: 但在只有52名参议员的情况下要向参议院提交法案，我认为你必须起草一个范围更窄的法案，然后在今年秋天回来，

sentences.en: and try to write a bill that can get 60 votes.
sentences.zh: 并尝试起草一个能够获得60票赞成的法案。

sentences.en: I don't think you can do both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这两件事可以同时做到。

sentences.en: But would it be better off to just repeal the Affordable Care Act rather than...
sentences.zh: 但是，直接废除《平价医疗法案》是不是比……

sentences.en: They couldn't.
sentences.zh: 他们做不到。

sentences.en: Rather than having...
sentences.zh: 与其拥有……

sentences.en: You couldn't get it through the Senate.
sentences.zh: 你在参议院通不过。

sentences.en: So it's okay to have as a foundation the Affordable Care Act that President Obama put in place?
sentences.zh: 所以，以奥巴马总统实施的《平价医疗法案》作为基础是可以的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: This is part one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一部分。

sentences.en: Everybody on the right said move immediately, okay?
sentences.zh: 右翼的所有人都说立即采取行动，对吧？

sentences.en: If you're going to move immediately with 52 senators, this is the most aggressive you can move.
sentences.zh: 如果你打算在只有52名参议员的情况下立即采取行动，这就是你所能采取的最激进的行动了。

sentences.en: Now, if you want to be patient and move in September or October, you may be able to round up 60 votes.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你想保持耐心并在9月或10月采取行动，你或许能争取到60票。

sentences.en: I also think once we get past repealing Obamacare, which will get no Democratic votes,
sentences.zh: 我还认为，一旦我们过了废除奥巴马医改这一关——这不会得到任何民主党人的投票——

sentences.en: the second step of transition away from Obamacare may actually be written in the manner where you start getting Democratic votes.
sentences.zh: 逐步摆脱奥巴马医改的第二步，实际上的起草方式可能会开始赢得民主党人的投票。

sentences.en: And you're going to have to get eight Democrats in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 而且你将必须争取参议院中八名民主党人的支持。

sentences.en: If you keep every Republican, you're going to have to get eight Democrats in the Senate to pass the bill.
sentences.zh: 如果你保住每一个共和党人，你将必须争取参议院中八名民主党人的支持才能通过法案。

sentences.en: If I thought this was the only bill, I'd be uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 如果我认为这是唯一的法案，我会感到不安。

sentences.en: I think this is the first step in a multi-step process.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是多步流程中的第一步。

sentences.en: And you do know something about getting laws passed in the United States Congress?
sentences.zh: 而你对在美国国会通过法律确实有所了解，对吧？

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 略知一二。

sentences.en: Once upon a time.
sentences.zh: 曾经。

sentences.en: Is America just not supposed to have a national health care system?
sentences.zh: 难道美国注定不应该拥有一个全国性的医疗保健系统吗？

sentences.en: America should have a system that guarantees that every American has access to health care,
sentences.zh: 美国应该拥有一个能够保证每个美国人都能获得医疗保健的系统，

sentences.en: but we are such a diverse country that we should, in fact, look at allowing states to develop models that fit those states.
sentences.zh: 但我们是一个如此多元化的国家，因此我们实际上应该考虑允许各州制定适合各州情况的模式。

sentences.en: Alaska is astonishingly different than Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加与罗德岛有着惊人的不同。

sentences.en: And to try to design one size fits all for this entire country, I think, would both be a mistake.
sentences.zh: 试图为整个国家设计一种放之四海而皆准的方案，我认为既是一个错误。

sentences.en: And if you're in the early stages of a radical scientific revolution, it also would mean bureaucrats slowing down every single new innovation.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你正处于一场激进科学革命的早期阶段，这也意味着官僚们会拖慢每一项新的创新。

sentences.en: Speaker Gingrich, thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 金里奇议长，非常感谢您接受采访。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: WikiLeaks is releasing what appears to be the largest leak of CIA documents in history,
sentences.zh: 维基解密正在公布据称是历史上最大规模的中央情报局文件泄密事件，

sentences.en: publicizing what it says is a secret set of tools the agency uses to break into smartphones, computers, and Internet-connected Tvs.
sentences.zh: 公开了它所称的该机构用于入侵智能手机、电脑和联网电视的一套秘密工具。

sentences.en: Those TVs can be turned into secret recording devices, even when they're switched off.
sentences.zh: 这些电视甚至在关机时也可以变成秘密录音设备。

sentences.en: The CIA has not confirmed the authenticity of the documents, but a government official tells The Times they are real.
sentences.zh: 中央情报局尚未证实这些文件的真实性，但一名政府官员告诉《时报》它们是真的。

sentences.en: And days after North Korea launched its latest missile test, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在朝鲜进行最新导弹试射几天后，美国

sentences.en: has begun deploying a missile defense system in South Korea.
sentences.zh: 已开始在韩国部署导弹防御系统。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: says the system will protect the South from the North, but China sees it differently.
sentences.zh: 表示该系统将保护南方免受北方威胁，但中国对此有不同的看法。

sentences.en: It's calling the U.S.
sentences.zh: 中国称美国的

sentences.en: move a provocative challenge to China's power in the region.
sentences.zh: 举动是对中国在该地区权力的挑衅性挑战。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For more of The Daily, text the word DAILY to 63937.
sentences.zh: 想要收听更多《每日新闻》，请发送短信 DAILY 到 63937。

sentences.en: I'll send you links to stories and some observations.
sentences.zh: 我会向你发送报道链接和一些观察意见。

sentences.en: Again, text the word DAILY to 63937.
sentences.zh: 再次提醒，发送短信 DAILY 到 63937。

sentences.en: And thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
